key_insight: A neural-hierarchical robotic skin combines densely packed iontronic touch sensors with fast readout and data compression. It enables humanoid robots to perceive fine textures, handle delicate objects and respond to potentially harmful contact.
problem_solved: Large-area robotic skins must capture detailed touch information while managing the data volume and processing demands of dense sensor arrays.
method: Use a high-density iontronic sensor array to capture detailed tactile signals.
Combine fast sensor readout with data compression to manage tactile information efficiently.
Organize processing in a neural-hierarchical architecture to support texture perception, delicate manipulation and responses to nociceptive stimuli.
impact: For embodied AI practitioners, this work connects high-resolution tactile sensing with efficient data handling. It could support more capable robot perception and safer interaction with fragile objects and surrounding environments.

paper_title: Large-scale iontronic skins with neural-hierarchical processing architecture
paper_authors: Zhibin Li, Bingxu Da, Junli Shi, Taihong Wang, Wenlong Si
